 ATP Paris Day 3 Predictions Including Alexander Zverev vs Lorenzo Musetti 
 Share Share this article
 × X Facebook LinkedIn WhatsApp Reddit Email Copy 
 Day three at ATP Paris with the second round due to be concluded in the French capital. As ever, we here at LWOT will be offering our predictions for every match on the slate, including Novak Djokovic vs Rinky Hijikata and Daniil Medvedev vs Ignacio Buse . But who will advance to the second round?
 ATP Paris Day 3 Predictions
 Alex de Minaur vs Tomas Martin Etcheverry
 Head-to-head: de Minaur 1-1 Etcheverry
 Tomas Martin Etcheverry arrives in Paris in the second round, battered but buoyant, after outlasting Andrey Rublev on Tuesday in a three-set grind that hinged on a barrage of 20 aces. It was just enough to get him over the line, but the Argentine will need to find another gear against Alex de Minaur, who offers far less margin for error than a wounded Rublev.
 Alex de Minaur, meanwhile, is riding the crest of a wave. His run to the Vienna final saw him knock out Tomas Machac, Learner Tien, Matteo Berrettini and world number one Alexander Zverev before Carlos Alcaraz finally stopped him. Those ranking points keep his Turin dream alive, and that hunger should fuel him this week. Writh two straight wins over Etcheverry already in his pocket, and barring any hangover from Vienna, the Australian’s pace and consistency should be too much. Expect de Minaur to win, and to do it comfortably.
 Prediction: de Minaur in 2 
 Frances Tiafoe vs Quentin Halys
 Head-to-head: first meeting
 Quentin Halys earned his stripes on Tuesday at the ATP Paris Masters, grinding past a stubborn Arthur Fery in a tight contest decided by a late break. The Frenchman backed his serve at key moments and finally broke through for his first main-draw win at this tournament on his eighth attempt, in front of the home crowd. That kind of breakthrough tends to travel with a player, and Halys will carry that belief into round two.
 Awaiting him is seventh seed Frances Tiafoe, whose form has cooled considerably since his US Open semi-final run. Tiafoe hasn’t won a match in Paris since reaching the quarter-finals in 2022, and his showings in Asia and Vienna did little to stir the imagination, so the question is which version turns up.
 The pair haven’t met on the ATP Tour, and their last clash came on the Challenger circuit in 2017, when Halys took three of four, though that tells us little now. Tiafoe is the favourite on paper, but with the crowd behind him and momentum on his side, Halys might just have enough to spring an upset.
 Prediction: Halys in 3

 Arthur Fils vs Tomas Machac
 Head-to-head: Fils 1-0 Machac
 Arthur Fils is in Paris with a point to prove and a question mark hanging over his body. The later start this week gave him extra time to shake off the physical issue that forced his retirement against Taylor Fritz in Basel, and he insists he’s fit and ready. Until he’s moving freely under the Bercy roof, though, that claim stays unproven. The stakes are clear: a few wins here would all but book his ticket to the ATP Finals in Turin, and with a home crowd behind him, the Frenchman has all the motivation he could ask for.
 Across the net at the ATP Paris Masters is Tomas Machac, who arrives battle-tested after two rounds of qualifying and a first-round win over fellow Frenchman Kyrian Jacquet. Three matches on these courts means he’s already dialled into the conditions and the surface, a small edge over a Fils who is stepping in cold. But Fils has played at a different level for much of 2026, and the firepower, the incentive and the crowd all favor him. Provided the body holds up, expect Fils to survive the early test and move on.
 Prediction: Fils in 2 
 Alexander Zverev vs Lorenzo Musetti
 Head-to-head: Musetti 3-2 Musetti
 Fresh from being officially crowned world #1, Alexander Zverev arrives in Paris with a point to prove . His form since the US Open triumph has been strong, with semi-finals in Shanghai and Vienna, and the Paris indoor hard courts have long been kind to him: champion in 2024, runner-up in 2020, and a semi-finalist in 2021 and last year. Few players in the draw can match his comfort in this building, and he will want to show the new ranking is no ceremonial title.
 Standing in his way on Wednesday at the ATP Paris Masters is Lorenzo Musetti, who edged Hubert Hurkacz 7-6 7-6 in a contest with almost nothing between them. The Italian never faced a break point in what he called one of his best serving displays, and he will need to reproduce that level to threaten Zverev. Musetti leads the head-to-head 3-2 and knows he can cause problems on his day, but Zverev won their latest meeting in Vienna last year and looks a clear step ahead right now. Barring rustiness or a complacent start, the German should find a way through.
 Prediction: Zverev in 3
